exposure: dietary deficiency of calcium and phosphorus
socio-demographic characteristics (residence in rural area, socio-economic class)
maternal calcium/vitamin D supplementation during pregnancy
outcome: rickets (prevalence, clinical presentation, radiological signs, biochemical laboratory findings)
cohort: A total of 500 children aged 0-14 years suspected of having rickets were enrolled in the study.
finding: The prevalence of rickets was 16%, being more prevalent in males aged 0-5 years, and vitamin D deficiency was found in 72.5% of children with rickets.
